patterns.evidence: Post-breakfast glucose peaks reach 222-278 mg/dL within 2 hours of morning meal on all 10 days from an already elevated fasting baseline. Average additional spike +88 mg/dL. High-GI breakfasts include cereal, bagels, pancakes, toast/jam/OJ, sugary oatmeal, smoothies, waffles. Even lower-carb D9 (eggs/toast) shows a 52 mg/dL rise.

analysis.message: This 20-year-old T1 patient demonstrates severe post-breakfast hyperglycemic spikes reaching 222-282 mg/dL daily. The 109kg weight drives high insulin requirements (basal 30L). Pre-bolusing 30 minutes before breakfast with an increased ICR of 1:5 would significantly reduce the morning peaks. Basal appears appropriately dosed given bedtime values 155-172 mg/dL. Weight management is crucial for long-term metabolic improvement. Metformin (off-label for T1) may improve hepatic insulin sensitivity.

analysis.message: This 49-year-old T1 patient demonstrates a highly predictable pattern of iatrogenic post-lunch hypoglycemia despite extreme obesity (120kg). The lunchtime ICR (currently ~1:7) is too aggressive for this patient's lunchtime insulin sensitivity. Reducing the lunchtime ICR to 1:12 would eliminate these daily events. Basal (34L) is appropriately dosed for 120kg. Weight management is crucial for long-term metabolic health and reducing total insulin requirements.

patterns.name: Post-Lunch Hypoglycemia
patterns.evidence: Consistent hypoglycemic events (58-72 mg/dL) occurring at 15:00-15:45 on all 10 days. Pre-lunch glucose is normal (112-128 mg/dL). Rescue carbohydrates required daily. Lunch bolus doses (2.5-3.5 units) appear excessive for the modest carbohydrate intake (15-30g). Despite extreme weight (120kg) requiring high basal insulin (34L), lunchtime insulin sensitivity appears unexpectedly high.
